session: One working session is one reviewable pull request with its checks: the unit the work of 25 and 26 November 2026 was done in.
basis: The only measured points are these: one authored building (Granada's watermill) with the pipeline that made it took two sessions; a playable prototype scenario with its rules, page, seven languages and scripted players took about three; a defect found by a reviewer was reproduced, fixed and released in two. Everything else is the author's estimate from those, and is uncertain by a factor of two or more. They are estimates of an agent's effort, never of calendar time: calendar time is set by reviewers, testers, the reference machines, the founder's answers, and runs that take four hours by the clock.

phases.title: Recorded and held
phases.what: The handoff, the founder's decisions, the inventory of the images, the regression scenarios on every release.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.what: What every later piece stands on: the shell, reach, measurement, layout, the keyboard, the ledger of history, the regression scripts.
phases.state: now, beside Granada's proof frame: these are shared by all three games

phases.title: Granada to its target
phases.what: First, by the founder's choice of 25 November 2026: a proof frame, then the economy, construction, estates, security, the map, the campaign, the art, Photo Mode, and after them first-person.
phases.state: the game in production now; its proof frame comes first, and nothing is made in number before the founder accepts it

phases.title: The Golden Age to its target
phases.what: The clock, the city, the economy, the Baghdad campaign, the art.
phases.state: after Granada reaches its gates. Before then only its proof frame may be explored

phases.title: Atlas to its target
phases.what: The terrain globe, the picture and clues, hints, layers and overlays, the local profile and Challenge.
phases.state: after The Golden Age. Before then only its proof frame, its pictures and its data licences

phases.title: A living world
phases.what: Day and night, weather, sound, movement that follows the game, in all three.
phases.state: woven into phases 2 to 4 as each game's art arrives

phases.title: People, machines and candidates
phases.what: Native readers, playtests, the reference machines, the soaks, the side-by-side with the targets, and the founder's approval.
phases.state: people and machines can be arranged from now; the runs follow each game's phase

packages.title: One shell for every game: one render loop and one audio graph, a tab in the background throttled and resumed, a lost graphics context recovered, an error state and a respectful message where a device is not supported
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 1; no blank canvas, duplicate loop or duplicate audio on any scripted path; mobile and tablet see the message, not a broken page

packages.title: Reach: the same renderer on WebGL 2 where there is no WebGPU; low, medium and high presets that keep the game and a coherent picture
packages.gate: Each required browser draws the game or says plainly why not; the three presets pass the same play scripts
packages.waitsOn: Whether the plan view alone counts as a pass on a browser without WebGPU is not asked: the aim is 3D on every required browser

packages.title: Measurement: frame times, memory and counts of contexts, textures, geometries, materials, render targets, timers, workers, listeners and audio nodes; a 60-minute repeated-action runner and a soak runner
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 9; a report per run with hardware, system, browser, size, preset, traces and memory

packages.title: Panels that hold from 1280 by 800 to 1920 by 1080, at pixel ratios 1 and 2, left to right and right to left
packages.gate: XG-03 scripted: nothing cut off, overlapping or out of reach at either size in English, Arabic and Urdu

packages.title: Saves that carry a version and are brought forward as systems are added, in all three games
packages.gate: XG-05; a save from each earlier release loads or is set aside, never half-loaded

packages.title: Media at scale: models, textures and globe tiles on the games host, with budgets and a visible loading state
packages.gate: A release with its media missing still plays; budgets written and checked in the build

packages.title: Photo Mode, Granada first: hide the interface, move, turn, zoom and focus, preview time of day and weather, capture, change nothing in the game
packages.gate: The founder's eight requirements for Photo Mode, each scripted; memory level after 50 entries and exits
packages.waitsOn: Required for the first production release

packages.title: First-person in Granada: walkable ground, collision, stairs, bridges, doors, no walking through water, walls, people or buildings, a safe way back
packages.gate: The founder's eight requirements for first-person, each scripted; no button for it is shown until they pass
packages.waitsOn: Required before Granada is called complete

packages.title: Granada's proof frame: one view of the running game built to the target's density and finish, with working panels, people at work, a selectable estate and a visible change of state, at three presets, with its measurements and what it cost to make
packages.gate: The fourteen lines of the proof-frame checklist; the founder accepts the direction
packages.waitsOn: The founder's acceptance. No asset is made in number before it

packages.title: Granada's buildings: the palace on its hill, walls, towers, gates and keep, town houses, the market, courtyard houses, the bridge, estate buildings, the oil press, the warehouse, the reservoir
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 2; every building in the catalogue has an authored model, a state under construction, and a place in the historical-review ledger
packages.waitsOn: Named reviewers for architecture

packages.title: Granada's land, water, planting, air and seasons to the target's density
packages.gate: Handoff prompts 2 and 7; the four seasons each set beside the target; the performance gates hold on the low preset

packages.title: Granada's people, animals, carts, boats and building sites, moving because the game moves them
packages.gate: GR-10 passes by sight for a reviewer who is not the author; each kind of movement is tied to a state of the game

packages.title: The Golden Age's city: houses, markets, bridges, boats, the water wheel, the scholarly buildings, cranes and scaffolding
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 4; every building in the catalogue has an authored model and a ledger entry
packages.waitsOn: Named reviewers for architecture

packages.title: Atlas's globe: relief, rivers, mountains, cloud, night lights and air, from data whose licence is checked
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 6; a statement of each data set's source and licence; no light or label gives an answer away
packages.waitsOn: The founder's approval of each data set, line by line (asked for Natural Earth and ETOPO 2022)

packages.title: Interface art for each game in its target's manner: icons, panels, type
packages.gate: XG-06 for the interface; contrast and focus pass

packages.title: Granada's economy: a second market, shipments that take time and cost, contracts, the olive oil chain, a marketplace with trend and demand
packages.gate: Corrective piece 2; no money made by a round trip; every sum on the page is the ledger's

packages.title: Granada's construction: a catalogue by category, placement with a preview that refuses bad ground, building over time with workers and materials
packages.gate: GR-07 in full: valid and invalid placement, collision, nothing lost on refusal

packages.title: Granada's estates: workers, irrigation, expected harvest, storage; water for three settlements
packages.gate: The estate panel's figures equal the rules' forecast

packages.title: Granada's defence as strategy, with no battle on screen: walls, gates and towers and their upkeep; readiness; reserves of food and water; supply routes; warnings from the border; tribute, negotiation and alliance; the people's confidence; consequences off screen; repair and recovery
packages.gate: Each can be raised or neglected with a consequence the player can explain; every event family is in the historical-review ledger
packages.waitsOn: Named reviewers. No combat unit, battlefield control or graphic violence without the founder's separate approval

packages.title: Granada's regional map and its layers; ports and routes
packages.gate: The map's distances are the museum's; each layer shows a real state

packages.title: Granada's objectives, journal and decisions; a prologue of 15 to 30 minutes, scenarios of 30 to 60, a campaign of three hours with several ways to win
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 3; scripted players show at least three strategies that can win and none that cannot lose; lengths confirmed by people, not by scripts
packages.waitsOn: Human playtests for length, clarity and enjoyment

packages.title: The Golden Age's clock: time that runs with speeds, building and research that take time, rates by the month
packages.gate: The forecast still equals what happens; a save from the season-by-season game is brought forward or set aside

packages.title: The Golden Age at the scale of a city: districts, a catalogue of six categories with Civic Resilience in place of Military, the new buildings, a city map
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 4; every catalogue item does something; no combat unit exists

packages.title: The Golden Age's economy: scaling and balance, trade and diplomacy, population, five city indices each with its causes
packages.gate: Corrective piece 5; GA-07 rewritten on purpose; no strategy wins every time

packages.title: The Golden Age's research and objectives, onboarding, chapters of 30 to 60 minutes, a campaign of three hours: 'a fictional city simulation inspired by records of Abbasid Baghdad and other historical institutions of the Islamic world', never called a reconstruction
packages.gate: Handoff prompts 4, 5 and 10; lengths confirmed by people
packages.waitsOn: Named reviewers; human playtests

packages.title: Atlas's round: a picture, three clues in turn, the period with a timeline, three kinds of hint each at a stated cost, the score in view
packages.gate: AT-03 and AT-04 for every hint; a clue never names the answer

packages.title: Atlas's layers: terrain, mountains, rivers; overlays tied to the period; modern borders only after the reveal, or as a hint with a stated cost
packages.gate: AT-06; a test that no layer open in an unanswered round shows a modern border

packages.title: Atlas's local profile and Challenge: personal bests on the device, themed challenges, a result to copy, pass-and-play, practice and expedition sessions
packages.gate: AT-08 and AT-09; nothing on any page implies scores are compared between people

packages.title: A living world in all three: day and night, weather, ambience and effects, movement that follows the game
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 7; XG-04; GR-11, GA-11

packages.title: The historical-review ledger: every statement of history a game makes, entered before it ships
packages.gate: No statement of history is on a page without a ledger entry; a check in the build
packages.waitsOn: Six named reviewers and the museum's editor, to move any entry from 'historical review pending'

packages.title: Granada's scenarios and campaign written from the museum's records
packages.gate: Every claim cites a museum record; fiction is labelled
packages.waitsOn: Named reviewers

packages.title: The Golden Age's Baghdad: what may be said of the city and its institutions, from the museum's records
packages.gate: Every claim cites a museum record; the district stays fictional and labelled until review
packages.waitsOn: Named reviewers

packages.title: Atlas's clues, themed collections and overlays from the museum's records; the picture collection: 48 more pictures through the museum's own media work, each through the ten requirements
packages.gate: 52 pictures that qualify before a weekly picture round is scheduled; three clues a round, none naming the answer
packages.waitsOn: The museum's media; the held V&A images; named reviewers for boundaries

packages.title: The keyboard everywhere: every panel reached and left, focus seen, shortcuts written down
packages.gate: XG-02 scripted for each game

packages.title: Names for a screen reader and a list or plan view of every new system
packages.gate: Each new system can be used from the plan view; a pass with VoiceOver by a person

packages.title: Seven languages for every new string, and each new panel laid out right to left
packages.gate: The strings check passes; XG-01 scripted

packages.title: Arabic and Urdu read by native speakers, then the other languages
packages.gate: At least three Arabic or Urdu testers; their corrections made
packages.waitsOn: Native readers of Arabic and Urdu, found by the founder

packages.title: Reduced motion, contrast and text size
packages.gate: WCAG 2.2 AA checks scripted where they can be

packages.title: The regression matrix on every release, with scripts for the 27 scenarios not yet fully covered
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 11; every scenario covered or marked as needing a person, with the evidence of each release kept

packages.title: Runs on the reference machines and browsers
packages.gate: The founder's performance gates on an M1 MacBook Air with 8 GB and a Windows 11 laptop with a Core i5-1135G7, in Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox as he listed
packages.waitsOn: A named operator for each of the two machines

packages.title: The 60-minute repeated-action profile and the four-hour soak of each game
packages.gate: Memory level after warm-up; any unexplained growth over 10% across identical cycles looked into; counts steady

packages.title: People playing: 5 to 8 for each game early, then 12 to 20 across the three, three or more of them reading Arabic or Urdu
packages.gate: Gates R10, R14 and GRA25, by the protocol
packages.waitsOn: Testers and a facilitator, found by the founder or a coordinator he appoints

packages.title: Each game set beside its target, frame by frame
packages.gate: XG-06, signed by the founder

packages.title: A production candidate's evidence, and the founder's approval
packages.gate: Handoff prompt 12; only then does a prototype label come off
packages.waitsOn: The founder

packages.title: The Golden Age's proof frame, by the same fourteen lines. Exploration may begin beside Granada; the frame is finished after Granada's lessons are written down
packages.gate: The proof-frame checklist; the founder accepts the direction
packages.waitsOn: The founder's acceptance

packages.title: Atlas's proof frame, by the same fourteen lines, with relief from approved data and cloud drawn by the game
packages.gate: The proof-frame checklist; the founder accepts the direction, and accepts or refuses the reveal in place of a group of people
packages.waitsOn: The founder's approval of the data sets, then his acceptance

packages.title: The hardware-test package: a benchmark mode in each game, the 60-minute and four-hour scripts, the page of the machine's facts, launchers and one page of instructions for a person who is not a developer
packages.gate: The package runs on a clean machine with no internet and writes one results file; two runs of the same address do the same thing
packages.waitsOn: Nothing to build it; operators to run it

packages.title: The words 'historical review pending' on the games' own pages wherever history is stated or linked, and the founder's sentence for The Golden Age, in seven languages
packages.gate: Every page of a game that states or links history carries the mark; the strings check passes; a release to UAT
packages.waitsOn: The founder's word for the UAT release

order.rule: Founder, 26 November 2026: production one game at a time, Granada, then The Golden Age, then Atlas, so that what Granada teaches about rendering, memory, simulation, interface and the art pipeline is applied to the other two. Full production of two games at once only with a separately staffed team for each.

stages.ends: The founder's approval of the evidence; then, separately, of deployment, and of the label

criticalPath.note: By the estimates, the engineering and art on this chain come to 41 to 76 sessions for Granada. The five steps that are people have no estimate at all, and nothing here can shorten them: reviewers, operators and testers are not yet named. They, not the engineering, set the date of Granada's first production release. The largest single uncertainty in the engineering is A1, the buildings, and it is unknown until the proof frame is judged.
